images.filename: Oileán Baoi (Dursey Island), Triangulation Pillar - geograph.org.uk - 283991.jpg
images.caption: Oileán Baoi (Dursey Island): Triangulation Pillar On a clear day like this one, the trig must have one of the finest aspects in all of Ireland. This view was taken looking back along the spine of Dursey Island towards the mainland, with the Kenmare River to the left and Bantry Bay to the right, but the views to the ends of the peninsulas to the north and south are equally spectacular. Cod's Head in V5447 is the headland to the left of the pillar. The pillar is at 252 metres above sea level.

images.caption:
Signal Tower, Dursey Island. The signal tower, said to be a relic of the defences erected during the Napoleonic wars, is here seen reflected in a small lochan on its western side. The Beara Peninsula stretches away to the east.
From this spot on a glorious clear day we could look to the north, the east and the south and see what seemed like the whole of the south west corner of Ireland; the peninsulas reaching out into the Atlantic, one behind the other, gradually fading into the blue haze.
